newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Hard-up Kazakh pensioners protest end of USSR.
newsitem.headline: Hard-up Kazakh pensioners protest end of USSR.

text.p: Pensioners, hard-hit by post-Soviet reforms, demonstrated in the centre of the Kazakh capital Almaty on Monday against the dissolution of the Soviet Union.
About 300 pensioners gathered on the capital's former Lenin Square in front of the Kazakh parliament. A statue of revolutionary leader Vladimir Lenin was removed from the square last year.
Demonstrations are rare in this resource-rich Central Asian republic where former Communist Party boss and now president Nursultan Nazarbayev has sweeping executive powers.
The unsanctioned rally was held to mark the sixth anniversary of an all-Union referendum held to try and save the already crumbling Soviet empire.
Most of those who voted in the referendum on the same day in 1991 voted "yes" to preserve the Union, although the vote was largely ignored in the republics of Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Moldova.

"People made their choice -- 95.6 percent, including President Nazarbayev, voted for the socialist development of Kazakhstan," said leaflets distributed at the rally organised by the Almaty-based Workers' Movement.
But the majority of the protesters appeared more worried about finding enough money to buy bread than a return to the certainties of the Soviet past.
"Yes, we understand it is impossible to return to the past," an elderly woman said. "But it is also impossible to suffer any longer," she said.
Nazikh Taipin, 76, said: "My pension is now only 2,800 tenge ($37) but after I pay the rent for my flat and utilities, only 300 tenge ($4) is left to live on.
"Can a human being live on this?" he asked.

Nazarbayev, worried by a fall in his popularity caused by late payments of meagre pensions and salaries, last week threatened to sack Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin if he did not improve the situation by April 10.
